Burn WKB geometries onto a regular grid.

Source: R/extendr-wrappers.R
cb_burn_wkb.Rd

Low-level worker behind cb_burn(). wkb is a list of raw vectors (one WKB blob per geometry, as produced by wk::wkb()). The grid is defined by its extent (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) and dimensions (ncol, nrow), with row 1 at the top (ymax edge). coverage = TRUE uses exact coverage fractions; FALSE uses the faster cell-centre (approx) rule.

Usage

cb_burn_wkb(
  wkb,
  xmin,
  ymin,
  xmax,
  ymax,
  ncol,
  nrow,
  coverage,
  parity,
  threads,
  id_offset,
  relate
)

Arguments

wkb

List of raw vectors, one WKB blob per geometry.

xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax

Grid extent.

ncol, nrow

Grid dimensions.

coverage

Logical; exact coverage fractions if TRUE, cell-centre rule if FALSE.

parity

Logical; if TRUE give the C++ core's records exactly: one run per fully covered boundary cell (no coalescing) and per-part records for multi-part geometries (no merging).

threads

Integer; number of threads, 0 for all available. With more than one the input is parsed up front, and the crate uses at most one thread per 8192 units of work, so small burns stay serial.

id_offset

Integer, non-negative; added to each geometry's position, so the id (and geom_index) columns are id_offset plus the 1-based input position.

relate

Logical; if TRUE also compute the DE-9IM relations of each polygon against the cells its boundary touches (see cb_relate()).

Value

A list of five lists (runs, edges, lines, points, notes), each a set of equal-length columns, and relations (the relations table if relate, otherwise NULL).

Details

Returns a list of five column-oriented tables: runs, edges, lines, points, and notes. The crate emits 0-based indices, half-open run ranges and id = k; this function converts to the R convention of 1-based row/col, inclusive col_end, and id/geom_index equal to the 1-based input position.
